## PMM: covariate adjustment

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
![](../excalidraw/PMM-013-Approaches_to_constrained_regression.excalidraw.svg){width="100%"}
:::

::: {.column width="42%"}
<div style="font-size: 0.5em; line-height: 1.2;">
Each cognitive test is regressed on the sociodemographic terms in the HRS/HCAP robust norms group. The coefficients describe expected performance for a person free of conditions that affect cognition, the same norming step as the Manly-Jones algorithm.

Three methods give the same adjustment: a residual from the norms-group equation, an offset, or fixed regression coefficients.

The Manly-Jones algorithm uses residuals. The PMM uses fixed coefficients, because five of the eight core cognitive tests are ordinal (ordered categories), and residuals do not work for ordinal tests.
</div>
:::
::::
